Course 08

History of the great schools

Ideas, influences and debates.

Lesson 1. Studying consciousness

1 · Lesson

The first schools of scientific psychology wanted to study consciousness. Structuralism, associated with Wilhelm Wundt and above all his student Edward Titchener, tried to break experience down into its basic elements (sensations, images, feelings) through trained, controlled introspection.

American functionalism, with William James and John Dewey, changed the question: not "what is the mind made of?" but "what is it for?". Influenced by Darwin, it saw consciousness as a tool for adaptation and took an interest in habits, education and individual differences.

Structuralism barely outlived Titchener, because introspection gave results that were hard to compare between laboratories. But it left the laboratory, measurement and the training of researchers. Functionalism left a practical psychology that paved the way for applied psychology.

2 · Example

A structuralist would ask which sensations make up the experience of hearing a chord. A functionalist would ask why we have the ability to distinguish chords and how it helps us find our way in the world. Same experience, different questions.

3 · Activity

For one minute, observe what you experience when tasting a food. Try describing it as a structuralist would (elements: taste, texture, temperature…). Then ask yourself, as a functionalist would, what each element is for.
